summary: This bill amends the Cranston-Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act to expand eligibility for affordable housing assistance to families earning up to 100 percent of the median income, allow more flexibility in how jurisdictions use housing funds, and streamline environmental review and other requirements for certain housing projects.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends existing housing acts to expand eligibility for housing assistance and infrastructure improvements, which would likely lead to increased federal outlays for housing programs. It also removes certain restrictions on how funds can be used and extends the period for drawing funds, potentially increasing the utilization of allocated funds.

The bill expands the definition of 'low-income families' to include those earning up to 100% of the median family income for housing assistance, and makes it easier for rental units to qualify as affordable housing if occupied by tenants with housing choice vouchers. These changes broaden access to housing assistance programs, which are a key component of the social safety net.
